correctness.rationale: The eight-letter-pair language of the four-symbol Rudin–Shapiro uniform morphism is closed under the substitution and all eight pairs occur in the fourth iterate; hence all factors at each specified length are exhausted by coding two adjacent substitution blocks. Complete exact partitions of the length-14 and length-18 factor sets show T² and T³ respectively have the same fibers as T; minimum one-counts are 3 and 5, meeting the prefix-inheritance hypotheses. For arbitrary longer factors, equality after deleting the first k ones implies equality of the first N prefixes under T^k; the base finite equivalence gives equality under T on the prefixes, and deletion-string equality forces identical remaining tails. This proves the infinite part. Concrete length-13 and length-17 pairs witness strict sharpness. Both Python verification programs reproduced all critical data, the second via an independent arithmetic word generator.

originality.rationale: The 2018 Defant–Kravitz paper defines the word operator; the April 2026 Campbell–Rampersad work treats iterated tortoise on the paperfolding word and a different one-step analysis on Thue–Morse. Neither inspected source gives Rudin–Shapiro two- and three-iterate fiber stabilization or exact thresholds 14 and 18. One-pass complexity alone cannot imply equality of these two higher-iterate partitions; the preceding-length counterexamples show they differ at adjacent parameters. Searches and accessible prior-claim comparisons identified no stronger equivalent or dominating claim, subject to normal unindexed-work priority risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 literature explicitly motivates iterated stack-sorting equivalence on automatic words. Iterating tortoise may merge previously distinct first-pass classes, so identifying when such additional merges disappear permanently is a natural invariant not determined by the one-pass complexity. The sharp lengths 14 and 18 exhibit an informative stability boundary in a classical automatic sequence, and the prefix-inheritance lemma offers a reusable route from exact morphic factor certificates to infinite all-length theorems. The result is not a mere small-n census: finite data are used as complete base certificates for an unbounded quantitative statement.
